text:
Alex: Quick postmortem from this morning's canary — saw a weird latency tail when a handful of late-join requests hit a nearly-full coalesce window. Noticed repeated soft preempts and an eventual hard flush that spiked p95.
Maria: ugh. do we have traces? can you paste the request ids? :eyes:
Alex: logs attached below (redacted). pattern: tenant A keeps late-joining 1-3 reqs to active window; scheduler tries soft-preempt -> moves them to fallback lane -> fallback batches are small -> KV cache eviction churn increases.
Sam: timeline from traces: 1) window open, 2) tenant A late-joins (deadline hint missing), 3) admission issues -> soft preempt attempts -> we call preempt handshake -> fallback path allocated -> batch size small -> slow token refill -> repeated flushes. p95 jumps.
Jen: sounds like two problems: late-join detection + preempted fallback shape. Could be headroom too. if we overcommit headroom for main lane, fallback starves.
Kai: Agree. I've been thinking about a "graceful-drain" handshake that lets late-joins declare intent + minimal deadline hint, then scheduler either: (a) accept into current window and extend deadline small (bounded), or (b) reject early and sequence into next micro-window with a priority tag. That avoids oscillation.
Alex: sketch of handshake (pseudo):
```
// client arrives w/ late_join=true
if (window.remaining_capacity > late_join_weight && window.age < max_age_for_extension) {
  extend_deadline(min(extension_limit, request.deadline_hint))
  mark_as_late_join
} else {
  route_to_next_microwindow(priority=late)
}
```
Sam: also we should bias fallback batching: don't let fallback lanes use naive timeouts. Use dynamic coalesce where microwindow waits for either N or deadline or a short jittered sleep that grows with backlog.
Maria: +1. For KV cache churn, we need to tie eviction policy to lane locality. If fallback lane evicts frequently we should warm a small sticky partition for that tenant.
Jen: that's storage-level. But on admission we can tag requests with cache affinity and prefer lanes that preserve KV residency.
Kai: tradeoffs: extending window delays main throughput and increases tail for all tenants vs pushing late-joins out increases p95 for those requests but keeps global latency. Which is more acceptable? Depends on SLOs.
Alex: for today I think we need a mitigation that's cheap: 1) add explicit late_join deadline_hint parsing and early rejection threshold, 2) jitter fallback microwindow wait to form slightly bigger batches, and 3) metric tagging to surface "late_join-induced preemptions".
Sam: agree. Also add a quick experiment: run canary with grace=5ms extension cap vs no-grace. measure p50/p95/p99 per-tenant.
Maria: we should also instrument KV eviction per-lane and track cold-warm transitions. currently metrics only show global evictions which hides hotspots.
Jen: new metric names proposed: runtime.lane.fallback.batch_size, runtime.lane.fallback.wait_ms, runtime.lane.late_join.count, runtime.kv.evictions.by_lane.
Alex: good. I'll open an infra ticket with those metric names + dashboard mock.
deploy-bot: canary deployed to i-rt-14 at 5321112244 :rocket:
Kai: one more thought — preempt handshake should be cancellable: if we decide to accept late join into extended window, we should cancel the fallback allocation immediately and re-credit tokens. avoids double allocation.
Sam: that needs accounting changes: token escrow vs final charge. we can implement a small escrow ledger keyed by window_id that keeps tentative allocations for X ms.
Alex: propose short-term rollout plan (3 steps):
- quick metrics + dashboard (Jen/Maria) 1 day
- implement deadline_hint parsing + early rejection + jittered fallback wait (Sam/Kai) 2-3 days
- add cancelable preempt handshake with escrow (Alex + Sam) 1 week
Jen: timeline works. Do we want a config flag per-cluster to toggle grace? yes.
Maria: add a chaos test: inject late-joins at 10% of traffic and verify no p95 spike > 20%.
Alex: action items: Alex create ticket for design + tests, Sam start on fallback coalesce change, Jen add metrics dashboard, Kai spec escrow API. I'll update thread with ticket IDs.
Sam: quick note — watch out for bursty tenants that might exploit extension to bypass rate limits; enforcement must be done post-handshake.
Alex: good call. rate limit check must run before any window extension.
Maria: thanks all. short follow-up sync in 30 if needed. :thumbsup:
